name: Acid, Vial
description:
A sealed vial holds one use of corrosive acid. As an action, splash it at a creature within five feet or throw it up to twenty feet. Resolve a ranged attack as an improvised weapon; a hit deals 2d6 acid damage.

The GM resolves the attack and damage manually. The use activity removes one vial; it does not roll an attack or apply damage. The vessel is destroyed or emptied by use.

weight.notes: Half a pound includes the filled vial and disposable stopper versus 1 lb officially. Project 15 gp keeps a dangerous prepared reagent a specialist purchase below the 25 gp reference.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants

use.condition: The GM resolves the described effect; using this activity only records charge or supply use.

name: Alchemist's Fire
description:
This sealed flask contains a sticky liquid that ignites on contact with air. As an action, throw it up to twenty feet and make a ranged attack as an improvised weapon. A hit causes 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of the target’s turns. The target can use an action to make a DC 10 Dexterity check to extinguish the flames.

The GM resolves the attack, recurring damage and extinguishing check manually. Using the activity removes one flask; it applies no ongoing effect or timer.

weight.notes: The filled flask weighs 0.7 lb versus 1 lb in the source. Project 30 gp retains a premium for a prepared persistent hazard relative to the 50 gp reference; no extra damage is granted.

name: Antitoxin
description:
One sealed dose is drunk to gain advantage on saving throws against poison for one hour. It provides no benefit to undead or constructs. It does not restore hit points, cure an existing condition automatically or guarantee immunity.

The use activity consumes the dose. The GM applies the saving-throw benefit and tracks its end manually.

weight.notes: The source lists no weight; 0.1 lb includes a small filled dose vial. Project 30 gp compares with the 50 gp reference and remains a significant prepared medicine purchase.

name: Ball Bearings
description:
A cloth bag contains one thousand small metal balls. Spreading the bag as an action covers a level ten-foot square. A creature moving through the area makes a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or falls prone; moving at half speed avoids the save.

The GM places the area and resolves movement and saves. Use removes one carried bag as a deployed supply, not one individual bearing. Recovered bearings must be recorded manually.

name: Caltrops
description:
Twenty iron caltrops fill one bag. An action spreads them over a five-foot square. A creature entering that area makes a DC 15 Dexterity save or stops moving this turn and takes one piercing damage; that damage reduces its walking speed by ten feet until it regains at least one hit point. Moving through at half speed avoids the save.

The GM resolves placement, saves, damage and movement. Use deploys the whole bag; it applies no terrain or condition automatically. Record recovered pieces manually.

weight.notes: The complete twenty-piece bag weighs 1.6 lb versus the 2 lb source unit. Project 7 sp compares with 1 gp and prices the bag, not each caltrop.

description:

The book is neither a spellbook nor a guarantee of correct or complete knowledge. The GM determines language, topic and any information an examination provides.

description:

description:
An iron jaw trap is attached by a chain, normally three feet long, to a secure anchor. An action sets it. A creature stepping on its plate makes a DC 13 Dexterity save or takes 1d4 piercing damage and stops moving. Thereafter, movement is limited by the chain.

A creature can use an action to attempt a DC 13 Strength check to free itself or another creature. Each failed attempt deals one piercing damage to the trapped creature. The GM resolves anchors, checks, placement and damage; the reusable activity changes no terrain or conditions.

weight.notes: Complete trap and chain weigh 18 lb versus 25 lb officially. Project 4 gp compares with 5 gp; the trap remains deliberately heavy and is excluded from a travelling wagon.

description:
One empty glass vial with a stopper holds four US fluid ounces. It is larger than the separate one-ounce apothecary vial. No potion, acid or other liquid is included.

The half-pound contents allowance is a project limit. Contents retain their own weight; the GM determines material compatibility and safe sealing.

weight.notes: Source weight is unspecified; 0.08 lb covers the empty four-ounce vessel and stopper. Project 1 sp compares with 1 gp and stays above the smaller 6 cp one-ounce vial.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants
source.reference: SRD 5.1 p. 69: Vial: 1 gp; weight not listed. Original wording and custom-economy price/adjusted weight. See docs/CORE_CATALOGUE.md.
